name: OpenTelemetry
certifications: OpenTelemetry Certified Associate (OTCA) - Linux Foundation / CNCF

beginner.summary: For developers, DevOps engineers and SREs who are new to OpenTelemetry and need to get useful telemetry out of real services. Covers the split between the OpenTelemetry API, SDK and Collector, the traces, metrics and logs signals, W3C Trace Context and baggage, zero-code instrumentation for Python, Java, Node.js and .NET, manual spans and metric instruments, log bridging, resources and semantic conventions, OTLP over gRPC and HTTP, a first Collector pipeline, exporting to Jaeger and Prometheus, head sampling, diagnosing missing telemetry, and a capstone that instruments a three-service application end to end.
prerequisites: Builds and runs a small web service in at least one of Python, Java, JavaScript/TypeScript or C#
Uses Docker and Docker Compose to start containers, read logs and expose ports
Understands HTTP requests, status codes and headers, and has a laptop with 8 GB of free RAM for the OpenTelemetry Demo
outcomes: Explain how the OpenTelemetry API, SDK, OTLP and the Collector fit together and which part owns which responsibility
Add zero-code and manual instrumentation to Python, Java, Node.js and .NET services and confirm that spans, metrics and logs reach a backend
Configure SDKs with OTEL_* environment variables, resources, propagators and head samplers so traces stay connected across services
Run a basic Collector pipeline that receives OTLP and exports traces to Jaeger and metrics to Prometheus, and diagnose common data-loss causes

intermediate.summary: For engineers who already instrument services with OpenTelemetry SDKs and now run the telemetry pipeline for a team or platform. Covers Collector components in depth, OTTL transformations, filtering and redaction, agent and gateway topologies, host, Kubernetes, Prometheus and file log collection, connectors such as spanmetrics and servicegraph, tail sampling and its load-balanced scale-out, resource detection, the OpenTelemetry Operator and its OpenTelemetryCollector and Instrumentation resources, k8sattributes enrichment, metrics SDK views and temporality, exemplars, context through messaging systems, Collector reliability and self-monitoring, and a capstone that builds a Kubernetes telemetry pipeline with the Operator.
prerequisites: Has completed the beginner level or can instrument a service with zero-code and manual OpenTelemetry and export OTLP to a Collector
Uses kubectl and Helm to deploy workloads, read logs and inspect resources on a Kubernetes cluster such as kind or minikube
Reads YAML confidently and can write PromQL queries with rate and sum by
outcomes: Design Collector pipelines that transform, filter, redact, enrich and route telemetry with OTTL and contrib processors
Deploy agent and gateway Collectors on Kubernetes with the OpenTelemetry Operator and inject zero-code instrumentation with Instrumentation resources
Apply tail sampling at scale with the loadbalancing exporter and derive RED metrics and service graphs with connectors
Run Collectors reliably with memory limits, persistent queues and internal telemetry alerts so data loss is detected and bounded

advanced.summary: For platform engineers, observability leads and instrumentation authors who own OpenTelemetry across many teams. Covers custom Collector distributions with OCB, writing Collector components and SDK extensions, authoring instrumentation libraries and Java agent extensions, eBPF zero-code instrumentation with OBI, the profiles signal, OpenTelemetry for GenAI and AI agents, custom semantic conventions with Weaver, declarative SDK configuration, OpAMP fleet management, Collector hardening, performance and overhead testing, multi-backend routing, migrations from older tracing stacks, cost and cardinality controls, organisational governance, large-scale pipeline diagnosis, and an enterprise platform capstone.
prerequisites: Has completed the intermediate level or runs OpenTelemetry Collectors on Kubernetes with tail sampling and the Operator
Writes Go well enough to build a module and read Go interfaces, and can read Java or Python library code
Has access to a Kubernetes cluster with at least 8 vCPU and 16 GB of RAM, and to an LLM API key or a local model server for the GenAI labs
outcomes: Build, extend and secure custom Collector distributions and manage Collector fleets remotely with OpAMP
Author instrumentation, SDK extensions and custom semantic conventions that follow OpenTelemetry specification rules
Instrument GenAI and agent workloads, eBPF-observed services and profiling data using current, clearly labelled development-stage conventions
Run an organisation-wide OpenTelemetry programme with performance budgets, cost and cardinality controls, migration plans and governance
